step1_summary: Chief complaint: Gradually worsening lower abdominal (suprapubic/below umbilicus) burning pain for 2 days, associated with feeling hot and sweaty.

Symptoms: Constant burning pain below the belly-button, began gradually 2 days ago, worsening; mild nausea (no vomiting); subjective fever/diaphoresis; ↑ urinary frequency; pink-tinged urine; no dysuria; bowels normal now (constipation last week, resolved); no diarrhea, no flank pain, no respiratory or cardiac symptoms.
Past medical history: Generally healthy; no previous surgeries; no similar episodes.
Medications/allergies: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) inserted 1 yr ago; no other meds; allergies not mentioned.

Gynecologic/sexual history: Sexually active with one partner (last intercourse 4 days ago); uses Implanon only; last menstrual period ~2 weeks ago; prior STI screen negative (6 months ago). Pregnancy possible though thought unlikely.
Social history: Non-smoker; social alcohol; lives in share-house; accountant.
Vital signs / exam: None recorded (telephone consult, no physical exam).
Labs / imaging: None yet (doctor suggested but not obtained).

V: Ovarian torsion: Acute lower abdominal pain can arise from vascular compromise of an ovary; constant worsening pain fits, though hematuria and urinary frequency are less typical.
I: Acute cystitis (lower urinary tract infection): Suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, pink urine, subjective fever match classic presentation.
Acute appendicitis: Early peri-umbilical pain becoming more focal, mild nausea, subjective fever could indicate evolving appendicitis.
Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID): Lower-abdominal pain, recent sexual activity, mild systemic symptoms; could precede vaginal discharge findings.
N: Bladder neoplasm: Hematuria with suprapubic discomfort, though age and acute course make this less likely.
D: Irritable bowel syndrome/functional bowel pain: Recurrent abdominal discomfort and bowel-habit changes, but acute onset and hematuria make this less likely.
I2: Implanon-related side-effects: Hormonal implant can cause irregular bleeding and abdominal discomfort.
C: Meckel’s diverticulitis: Congenital remnant can inflame and give periumbilical pain, but rare.
A: Endometriosis: Cyclical lower-abdominal pain but timing (mid-cycle) and hematuria make it less likely.
T: Ureteric/renal stone: Can give hematuria and abdominal pain, though typically colicky and radiating from flank.
E: Ectopic pregnancy: Lower-abdominal pain several weeks after last period, possible light bleeding mistaken as hematuria; life-threatening to rule out.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Acute cystitis (uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic triad of suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, and hematuria; mild systemic features without flank pain supports localized bladder infection.
Peri-umbilical/infra-umbilical pain, gradual worsening, mild nausea and subjective fever could represent early or atypical appendicitis.
Any reproductive-age patient with lower-abdominal pain warrants exclusion; Implanon reduces but does not eliminate risk; last period 2 weeks ago gives uncertain dating.
Lower-abdomen pain and systemic symptoms in a sexually active woman, but absence of vaginal discharge or cervical motion tenderness makes it less convincing.
Hematuria aligns, yet pain is constant suprapubic without flank radiation and no colic, so less likely.

opposing_evidence: No dysuria/burning on micturition (common with cystitis but can be absent)
No urinalysis yet to confirm pyuria/bacteriuria
Pain described as burning rather than colicky/sharp
No localization to right lower quadrant reported

supporting_evidence: Female of reproductive age, sexually active, no barrier contraception
Lower abdominal pain, could mimic hematuria if light vaginal bleeding unnoticed
Sexually active woman with lower-abdominal pain
opposing_evidence: No vaginal discharge, dyspareunia, or cervical motion tenderness noted
STD screen negative 6 months ago and single partner
Pain not colicky, no flank or groin radiation
No severe sudden onset or restlessness typical of colic
